questions: Should the KDE plots be generated for all columns, or only for columns that underwent Box-Cox transformation (i.e., non-constant columns)?

What should be done if a column's data after replacement is entirely zeros (i.e., no values match TARGET_VALUES)? Is that considered constant (so no Box-Cox) or non-constant (so Box-Cox after adding 1)?
Is the Box-Cox transformation applied to each column independently, and if so, should the lambda parameter be estimated per column (as in scipy's default) or fixed?
Should the KDE plots be displayed (plt.show()) within the function, or just the figure object returned without displaying?
What should happen if a column's data after replacement is constant but not zero (e.g., all 3s)? Should it still be plotted in the KDE figure?
Are the TARGET_VALUES considered as exact matches (including type, e.g., int vs float), or should numeric equality be used?
Should the function raise an error if the DataFrame contains non-positive values before replacement, or after replacement?
If a column is constant after replacement, should it be added to transformed_df unchanged (as in reference), or should it be omitted from transformed_df?
